entries.reason: IbkrBroker.spec.ts:1-87 bypasses construction with Object.create, casts private fields, and records raw SDK objects; the target replaces that as the conformance path with a scoped IbkrTestPort/callback codec, keeps Public fixtures account-free, and limits a durable TestJournalPort to controlled-effect crash cases.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:89-118 compares conId, routing, display, currency, tradingClass, and multiplier on the sent Contract; the target preserves every corpus field as immutable schema/fingerprint evidence and requires a separate explicit AccountScope before an effect dispatch.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:120-158 and IbkrBroker.ts:322-348 establish conId-only lookup, polluted-input isolation, canonical CASH routing, and retry after rejected lookup; the target keeps the Public InstrumentId resolver and makes display fields non-authoritative while effects bind scope independently.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:160-176 and IbkrBroker.ts:350-381 prove STK/SMART/USD defaults are applied to a clone for symbol convenience; the target confines that behavior to read-only ConvenienceStockQuery and makes unresolved symbol writes ResolutionRequired.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:178-191 and IbkrBroker.ts:369-381 reject incomplete CASH/non-STK routing before any bridge or EClient call; the target retains zero-wire validation, requires a resolved canonical identity for effects, and does not treat a no-conId routed read as an executable order.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:193-204 and IbkrBroker.ts:315-320 establish one concurrent conId lookup with independent returned ownership; the target correctly scopes the resolver flight by connection/generation and Public data scope, decodes immutable records, and avoids an account field on this public leaf.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:206-216 and IbkrBroker.ts:340-347 show a rejected first lookup is evicted so a later call retries; the target preserves that provider optimization with typed TransportUnavailable/ResponseMalformed/NoCanonicalMatch/StaleGeneration outcomes instead of caching transport failure as NoMatch.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:218-240 proves canonical routing during modify while IbkrBroker.ts:509-543 mutates a fetched native order in place; the target replaces Partial<Order> mutation with a scoped before-image/versioned exact patch schema and rejects omitted variants rather than dropping fields.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:242-259 and IbkrBroker.ts:561-585 show opposite-side market-DAY close, canonical IDEALPRO routing, and source-contract non-mutation; the target adds explicit AccountScope, ExposureSnapshot/version, All|Exact quantity, and residual/unknown recovery without making the cache authoritative.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:262-289 and IbkrBroker.ts:480-489 refuse populated TP/SL before bridge access while an empty object is effectively absent; the target exposes only ProtectionSpec=None, keeps protected variants absent with availability separate, and forbids a protected request from becoming a naked entry.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:291-325 proves conId precedence, issuer-directory refusal, symbol convenience, and key round trips; the target brands Leaf/IssuerDirectory/SymbolQuery, keeps resolved instruments Public, and requires explicit effect AccountScope instead of treating a directory or symbol as trade identity.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:327-387 and IbkrBroker.ts:606-660 establish mixed-currency conversion, finite broker NetLiquidation precedence, and no blind foreign sum without FX; the target carries AccountScope, typed Money/FxObservation provenance, and BrokerFact/Reconstructed/Unknown valuation states.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:389-473 and IbkrBroker.ts:701-757 establish positive bid/ask midpoint, multiplier-aware value/PnL, coalescing, TTL, and option-only refresh; the target makes marks AccountScoped with Fresh/Stale/Unavailable quality and bounded generation-aware flights without granting order authority.

IbkrBroker.spec.ts:475-535 and IbkrBroker.ts:141-162 prove known-dead rejection and the same-socket currentTime probe before native writes; the target retains no-wire-on-probe-failure, but gates send on durable DispatchStarted CAS and classifies post-send loss as Unknown rather than claiming the probe proved acceptance.

IbkrBroker.ts:1-47 is a single Promise-based class coupling SDK, lifecycle, reads, writes, and identity; the historical broker-spi ownership comparison is pinned at Git a5f23756531cc552b7e12b6d655ae1ffbcd28b64, and the target splits provider-declared leaves while preserving native authority inside the adapter.

IbkrBroker.ts:49-71 deep-copies combo legs and delta-neutral data before EClient ownership; the target preserves that safety behavior through an adapter-private NativeContractCodec and carries exact provider-declared extensions/child records as fingerprinted serializable records, never SDK instances.

IbkrBroker.ts:73-90 and ibkr-types.ts:13-24 expose optional primitive config and a paper label without environment observation; the target refines endpoint/client/selector data, treats Declared environment as intent only, and enables writes only after matching observed endpoint/account evidence, retaining the empirical question.

IbkrBroker.ts:92-102 makes fromConfig allocate a mutable broker directly; the target moves that side effect into scoped composition, separates Public handles from Account/effect handles, and leaves no ambient mutable IBroker constructor as authority.

IbkrBroker.ts:104-131 stores mutable connection state and conId/option caches on one object; the target scopes Layer state by generation, uses Public versus explicit AccountScoped keys, bounds/invalidate caches, and leaves dispatch identity/projections in durable stores.

IbkrBroker.ts:133-167 separates known-dead reads from a write-time currentTime probe; the target represents Alive/Dead/RestoredHint/Degraded with connection-generation evidence and permits dispatch only through the current durable lease/CAS, not probe success alone.

IbkrBroker.ts:169-180 uses a 45-second timer and 5-second currentTime probe with warning/dead marking; the target keeps those timings in a scoped supervised HeartbeatSupervisor, fences late generations, and routes started effects to observation instead of mutation retry.

IbkrBroker.ts:182-223 selects configured or first managed account, requests delayed data, and waits for the first account download; the target retains delayed-data/private-read barriers, preserves the full managed directory, and requires explicit AccountScope while retaining the sub-account/jurisdiction evidence question.

IbkrBroker.ts:225-229 only clears heartbeat, unsubscribes account updates, and disconnects; the target adds ordered admission stop, scoped interruption, Deferred completion, writer drain, and durable Unknown classification without turning data-reader cancellation into compensation.

IbkrBroker.ts:231-267 and request-bridge.ts:519-523 establish dot-suffix filtering, CASH expansion, BOND hub passthrough, and raw symbol samples; the target keeps these as Public typed search rows with leaf/hub identity, provenance, and Partial/Unavailable outcomes rather than exposing SDK objects.

IbkrBroker.ts:269-287 catches every CASH expansion error and returns []; the target correctly distinguishes a completed empty ContractDetails result (NoMatch) from transport, timeout, malformed, or entitlement ExpansionUnavailable, with no transaction WAL for ordinary data.

IbkrBroker.ts:289-313 returns the first ContractDetails row or null while propagating collector rejection; the target keeps first-row convenience only for explicit read queries and exposes Found/NoMatch/QueryFailure/AmbiguousIdentity with Public request evidence.

IbkrBroker.ts:294-313 clones query input, applies SMART/USD only to no-conId STK requests, and seeds the local cache; the target makes query kind explicit, keeps every query Public, and forbids defaults on conId, issuer, CASH, or routed-security queries.

IbkrBroker.ts:315-320 first-wins a numeric conId cache without eviction; the target retains insert-if-absent coalescing only for generation/schema-matching Public immutable records, bounds it at 256 entries/5 minutes, and never treats it as plan authority.

IbkrBroker.ts:322-348 requires an exact conId response, clones it, and deletes only the rejected matching promise; the target preserves these facts in a Public typed resolver with generation/schema fencing and separates NoMatch from transport or malformed failure.

IbkrBroker.ts:350-381 preserves canonical conId routing, STK convenience, and loud non-STK refusal while carrying aliceId; the target keeps aliceId as UntrustedAlias evidence, maps only resolved Public identity into routing, and requires explicit AccountScope for effects.

IbkrBroker.ts:384-476 implements issuer/underlying expansion, stable filtering, limit clamping, and option grids; the target preserves those transformations as Public typed leaves with explicit Complete/Truncated coverage, reissue boundaries, NoMatch, and ExpansionUnavailable instead of a fabricated cursor.

IbkrBroker.ts:478-507 and request-bridge.ts:231-242 expose immediate raw order mutation with openOrder acknowledgement; the target adds an exact provider placement schema/HOF, omits unsupported variants from input, preserves MOC/LOC/MOO/LOO-OPG and REL native mappings, and retains unanswered idempotency, acceptance, and percentOffset-unit questions as capability gates.

IbkrBroker.ts:509-543 mutates Partial<Order> in place and reuses numeric orderId; the target keeps provider-supported identity but requires a scoped before-image/versioned exact replacement schema, rejects schema-absent fields, and observes unknown sends without duplicate replacement.

IbkrBroker.ts:545-559 and request-bridge.ts:233-241,738-777 show cancel can resolve on openOrder or a synthetic Cancelled state; the target retains permId/clientId as Present|Absent native evidence and requires matching AccountScope/identity plus cancellation criterion, so synthetic state cannot confirm cancellation.

IbkrBroker.ts:561-585 and the FX close test preserve opposite-side market-DAY closure with canonical cloned routing; the target makes it an AccountScoped exposure effect with version/CAS, explicit quantity, and residual/Unknown recovery instead of display-symbol/cache authority.

IbkrBroker.ts:598-604 reads ExchangeRate rows as Decimal/null but accepts zero, negative, and non-finite values; the target emits PositiveFiniteDecimal or typed UnknownFx with AccountScope, receipt time, and provenance, never rate 1 or an implicit fallback.

ibkr-types.ts:46-50 and request-bridge.ts:644-678 show AccountDownloadResult has no provider timestamp/sequence and only swaps pending/live buffers; the target injects explicitly labeled adapter receipt time plus generation-local sequence, preserves account/currency provenance, and never claims venue ordering.

IbkrBroker.ts:662-699 refreshes only OPT/FOP rows with a hard cap of eight and leaves other positions untouched; the target preserves that policy while publishing AccountScoped Complete/Partial/Unavailable position observations and visible per-mark quality.

IbkrBroker.ts:701-722 uses conId success/failure TTL and finally-cleared in-flight promises; the target scopes Fresh/Stale/Unavailable cache entries by AccountScope, InstrumentId, and generation, retaining 15s/60s policy only as a data optimization.

IbkrBroker.ts:724-757 validates positive finite bid/ask and multiplier math but catches every error into a 60-second null cache; the target keeps expected unavailable negative TTL/old-mark retention while surfacing malformed callbacks and adapter defects as typed failures.

IbkrBroker.ts:759-775 and request-bridge.ts:244-269 cover only current-client open orders through single-slot collectors, while packages/ibkr/src/client/orders.ts:18-28 merely declares broader requests; the target makes listing results explicitly AccountScoped Complete/Partial/Unavailable and retains runtime permission/namespace completeness as an empirical gate.

IbkrBroker.ts:777-798 uses open-then-completed lookup and ephemeral fill enrichment, while request-bridge.ts:738-797 drops orderStatus permId/clientId; the target preserves lookup order but requires scoped identity/completeness evidence and maps partial absence to Unavailable/Unknown rather than null or rejection.

IbkrBroker.ts:800-839 and request-bridge.ts:680-734 prove snapshot=true, regulatorySnapshot=false, delayed tick handling, and zero defaults; the target preserves request flags but decodes Public quote field absence/quality explicitly and never treats Delayed or a snapshot as write authority.

IbkrBroker.ts:841-870 uses TWS currentTime then local NYSE weekday fallback, while the README documents distinct sessions/overnight freezes; the target makes the leaf Public and venue/instrument/session-aware, with the legacy fallback query-only and the calendar evidence question retained for writes.

IbkrBroker.ts:872-879 returns fixed security/order arrays for every context; the target retains them as AdvertisedCandidate evidence, derives per-leaf descriptors/availability from account and environment observations, and does not synthesize a global action map or infer permissions.

IbkrBroker.ts:881-918 defines conId, issuer, and symbol key grammar with STK defaults; the target version-encodes the identity ADT, makes issuer expansion and symbol lookup discovery-only, and binds resolved Public identity to explicit AccountScope/jurisdiction before effects.

ibkr-contracts.ts:47-77 and request-bridge.ts:488-517 combine numeric branches, regexes, swallowed informational codes, and UNKNOWN; the target preserves 2100-2199 diagnostics and 1100/1101/1102 health semantics, uses checked context mappings, and keeps unknown 10xxx codes operator-visible with no resend while retaining the code-table question.

ibkr-types.ts:13-24 repeats optional endpoint/account primitives, paper-port comments, and first-account behavior; the target uses refined connection/environment/selector ADTs, preserves every managed account, requires full explicit AccountScope for dependent leaves, and retains the missing sub-account/environment evidence question.

ibkr-types.ts:35-44 models ticks as optional raw numbers; the target maps them to Public QuoteObservation field-availability and Live/Delayed/Stale quality, preserving absent versus real zero and the tickSnapshotEnd barrier.

ibkr-types.ts:46-50 and request-bridge.ts:644-678 use Map<string,string> plus mutable positions and atomic cache swap; the target keeps composite currency/account evidence and checkpoint semantics in immutable AccountScoped observations, with rebuildable adapter buffers and no data WAL.
